what_happened: First timing harness bound the measured value with a pure 'let' and read the clock before any IO forced it; Lean floated the computation past the second clock read, so every stage reported 0 ms and five probe rounds chased phantom hangs. Fixed by emitting the value through an IO write before reading the clock.

A hoisted mirror of the backward liveness stack (posAt precomputed per time, verts shared) reduced the full bwdLiveT fixpoint at certA from an unfinished multi-hour run to 7.17 s, confirming recomputation rather than divergence as the cause.

certA.Certifies proved by kernel decide in 91 s with maxHeartbeats 0, after the same statement failed to return in 560 s under #eval. The task's blocking premise was an artifact of measuring the one evaluation path that cannot share closed subterms; the Tier-2 inventory row needs no library change.

certB.Certifies by decide had not returned after 13 minutes of a 3000 s budget, so the second Tier-2 row is left unconfirmed by this dispatch. certB's closure is roughly an order of magnitude larger than certA's in 2^|closure|.

Plan-time mechanical check found that the research report's recommendation 1 (land certA as the C36 Tier-2 inventory row) is not executable as written: C36b's c36Sliced interest expression requires a formula of the claimed kind to occur in G.slab t w, and certA's slice labelling carries only 'atom p', so c36Sliced evaluates false for snce, stab and imp alike (verified by compiled #eval against the built library). The plan therefore carries a slab-carrying variant of certA plus a decision gate, rather than the report's bare 'add the row' step.

Plan-time compiled probe confirmed the deliverable is reachable with one minimal repair: adding snceP to certA's slice labelling makes c36Sliced [c36Snce] true AND certA.Certifies still proves by kernel decide in 87 s total wall clock under an explicit finite maxHeartbeats 2000000 (not 0), which also discharges the research report's 'prefer a finite cap' risk mitigation. The plan's Phase 2 therefore rests on a this-round measurement rather than a carried figure.

lean-challenge-snapshot.sh's Goals parser is stricter than the plan-format examples suggest: it requires a column-0 '**Goals**:' line (not the '- **Goals**:' list-item form that landed sibling lean4 plans use) and extracts EVERY backticked single-word token in the Goals range, so a backticked namespace name ('Nu', 'EUFix') or ordinary prose word ('witness', 'true') is read as a committed identifier and fails cross-validation. Resolved by de-backticking all non-identifier prose in the Goals range and using bare undotted identifiers; the tool then exits 0.

Phase 1 baseline reproduced every carried figure from the research report within 1.12x (verts 9ms, bwdLiveT 1704 vs 1614ms, liveAt(-1) 20225ms vs 20.7s, certA verts 1114 vs 1101ms, 16 predT 18936 vs 19119ms), and both plan-time verdicts re-confirmed: c36Sliced [c36Snce] certA = true, and certA.Certifies proves by kernel decide in 43.4s under maxHeartbeats 2000000 -- faster than the plan's 87s figure.

First Examples.lean build failed: a docstring placed BEFORE 'set_option maxRecDepth ... in / set_option maxHeartbeats ... in' is a parse error ('unexpected token set_option; expected lemma'). The set_options must come first, and Mathlib's maxHeartbeats style linter additionally requires an explanatory comment between the set_option line and the declaration. Fixed in one edit; chained set_option ... in lines are otherwise fine.

The research report's carried 16.7x early-exit factor did not reproduce as a single number: measured 12.8x on bwdLiveStep (1563 -> 122 ms) but only 3.5x on fwdLiveStep (7606 -> 2177 ms), and the forward direction is the expensive one. Recorded in progress-file.md as superseding the report; later phases cite this round's figures.

Switching the four liveness fixpoints onto the early-exit forms cut the embedded witness's liveAt(-1) from 20225 ms to 1648 ms (12.3x), fwdLiveT 11.7x, bwdLiveT 9.3x, with every cardinality unchanged. The in-library factor exceeds the isolated probe-17 factor (3.5x on fwdLiveStep) because the inner untlLive/snceLive fixpoint is switched too and the two savings compound.

Phase 4's blast radius was one file wider than the plan-time grep found: FixtureStable.lean carries 'rw [untlLive]', which after the switch unfolded to lfp' and made EUFix.lfp_induction unify through lfp', hitting the 200000-heartbeat whnf timeout. It is not a direct dependent of LiveFix.lean so 'grep -rln PlusSlicedCertificate.LiveFix' missed it. A repo-wide grep over all twelve definitional-unfold spellings found the complete repair set (3 sites in 2 files).

Phase 5's hoist is NEUTRAL under the kernel, not the win the report's #eval figures implied. An A/B at one library state (both clause shapes run against the same build, no rebuild confound) measured 25.9 s OLD vs 24.4 s NEW on certA's backward fixpoint under decide -- 1.06x, inside variance. The kernel's whnf cache was already removing most of the per-vertex duplication. Under #eval the hoist is 5.4x better at certA but 25% WORSE at the small embedded witness, because the table's fixed |closure|-eager-evaluation cost dominates when the inner fixpoint is cheap. This is D4's hazard realized one phase before the gate that was designed for it.

Leaving untlLiveAt/snceLiveAt in the library untouched while adding untlLiveAtTab/snceLiveAtTab made a zero-rebuild A/B possible: both clause shapes run against one built library in two scratch decide files, so the comparison carries no machine-variance or rebuild confound. That is a far better evidence tier than the module-build wall clock, which moved 34->41 s for reasons the A/B shows are not the hoist.
